html:
The Kingdom of Loango was a state of the Vili people on the Atlantic coast of what is now the Republic of the Congo, flourishing from about the 1500s to the late 1800s.

Its kings ruled from Buali near the bay of Loango and traded ivory, copper, raffia cloth and redwood dye with Dutch and Portuguese ships. In the 18th century it became one of the main ports of the Atlantic slave trade north of the Congo river, sending captives brought from far inland by Vili caravans.

The trade made Vili merchants powerful and weakened the king. By the 19th century royal authority had faded, and in 1883 the coast came under French protection. Its old trade routes set the line later followed by the Congo to Ocean railway and the port of Pointe-Noire.
sum: The Kingdom of Loango was a state of the Vili people on the Atlantic coast of what is now the Republic of the Congo, flourishing from about the 1500s to the late 1800s.
